_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_status: Sam answered the sky's eight design calls in one sitting — eight of eight yes, no notes — and the Sky went in the same evening (PR #1514). SkyView now opens as the night sky seen through a window: Sky, Globe and Map are three words in the control row and three places to stand on the one canvas; the sky is dark by default and Day is one control away, with every dot rimmed so it still exists on the blue; it turns slowly until you touch it; a course drags and drops on the curve exactly as it did on the flat map; the CTE disciplines gather on one side of the sky and the academic ones on the other. What is left for Sam is his eye on it — and whether it moves smoothly on his machine, which nothing here can measure. Next session picks up from there.

items.text: The Sky is in. Open SkyView: it now opens as the night sky through a window, with Globe and Map one click away in the same row (Sky · Globe · Map). Every one of your eight answers is built as written — night by default and Day keeping the rim, the slow turn that stops at your first touch, drag-and-drop on the curve, the CTE side and the academic side with their two names, silver stars for the M-IDs. Two things only you can tell us: does it look the way you pictured it, and does it move smoothly on your machine? Our only measurement is from a headless test browser with no graphics card (about 13 frames a second at the opening window); your screen should do better, and if it does not, say so — there is a known next step.

The CPL face and the light are on the map — open SkyView, press CPL and Articulations, or use the link #skyview/cpl. Two questions only you can answer: does the credential-led label read right at your zoom, and is Articulations the word you want on the button? Everything else on the face follows your eight rulings as written.

The coverage sentence on the sheet said 1,490 of 6,388 exhibits. Both numbers were from the wrong bucket: 1,490 is the count of courses that carry an articulation (the exhibits are 1,924), and 6,388 is the credit funnel, which shares only 570 exhibits with the articulated ones — it is the military record, and the articulations are mostly industry certifications and credit by exam. The map says 1,924 of 5,497 articulated exhibits, computed from the data rather than typed in. Say if you would rather it also named how many of those the funnel has acted on (536).

Your ruling on where skill statements come from unblocked the course outline's skills layer — published agency standards are the text of record, an ACE exhibit fills a gap they leave, the MAP team overrides either, and a genuine conflict shows both side by side. But we hold none of that text: of 1,987 credentials classified, 64 of them welding, not one carries a skill field. So this is now a fetching problem, not a decision. The question for you is which published standard to start with — an AWS welding certification is the natural pilot.

You asked for a magic phrase people type before they can move a course, shifting to a team phrase later. That would be the first time anything is written from the map, which today writes nothing at all — so it goes through Governance and the privacy review before it ships rather than after. DR-24 now carries your name as its owner; say the word and the phrase gets scoped.

Only if Sam says the Sky drags: measure on the served page first (a draw costs 42 milliseconds in software rendering after the star pass was batched), then draw the small stars to an offscreen layer that is redrawn only when the view moves, or move the point pass to WebGL behind the same projection — never per-point work. The drop test, the keyboard path and the accessibility run go again in the same change; item 1 of the sheet made that the condition for the Sky opening at all.

DR-24 is a governance row with an owner and no surface yet: an added skill lands as proposed with the reviewer's name and the day, and joins the published outline when a second curator agrees; a removal works the same way in reverse. Building that means the map's first write, so it routes through Governance and the privacy review first.

Two housekeeping items behind the CPL face. Fifty-five exhibits in the articulation crosswalk are no longer in today's MAP feed; they stay on the map flagged in words rather than dropped, and the fix is a re-seed of the crosswalk from a fresh custom report. And the credit-funnel numbers the face carries for context were read by hand on 2026-09-07; refresh them after the next custom-report load.

Decision packs still only exist for 5 of the 159 disciplines because they are baked into the page. Fetching them per discipline the way the course descriptions already are is the bottleneck behind several of the remaining asks.
